approach.label: How we think
approach.title: Most studios ask what you want built. We ask who shows up first.
approach.subtitle: A two-sided product is worthless on launch day and nobody warns you. Owners won't join without renters. Renters won't join without owners. Clubs won't pay for a network with three clubs in it. We start there, before a single screen exists – because that's the question that decides whether the thing lives.

quote.body: The empty platform is the first product state we design for.

1.title: Every platform we built launched empty
1.desc: No listings, no members, no other side. We know what breaks in month two and which features you'll wish you'd cut. That's what you're hiring – not a framework list.

2.title: We'll tell you not to build it
2.desc: Sometimes the answer is a spreadsheet, an existing tool, or waiting. We'd rather lose the project on the first call than watch it die at month five. Ask for an example – we'll name one.

3.title: Same timezone, EU contracts
3.desc: Poznań, Poland. An EU entity your legal team can contract with, data and IP handled inside the EU, and a team working your hours. Nobody schedules a 6am standup.

about.title: We ask hard questions before we open Figma.

faq.title: Questions that decide whether we should work together
faq.subtitle: Straight answers before either side spends time on a proposal.

cta.sub: We're happy to answer them directly.

faq.q1: Will you build my Uber for X?
faq.a1: Maybe. But on the first call we'll ask which side you can get 100 of by hand, without ads. If there's no answer, the product isn't ready and we'll say so instead of taking the money.
faq.a2: Because a fourth would be a claim we can't back with work yet – we're building our first agritech platform now and we'll say so plainly until it ships. We build platforms where participants have to find and trust each other. That shape repeats across marketplaces, clubs and logistics. Outside it we'd be guessing on your budget.
faq.q3: How much does a platform cost?
faq.a3: It depends on the trust model, number of participant roles and operational tooling. We'll give you a rough budget range on the first call and a fixed price after scope. If a prototype is the smarter first step, we'll say so.
faq.q4: Can I hire you for just design, or just development?
faq.a4: Yes. Design-only, build-only, or marketing-only all work. We'll scope it accordingly.
faq.q5: Do you work with existing codebases?
faq.a5: Yes. We'll audit first and give you an honest verdict, including "rewrite" or "keep your current team."
faq.q6: What does working together look like?
faq.a6: Discovery → design → build → launch. One-week sprints, a demo every sprint. You always know what shipped and what's next.
faq.a7: Retainers for ongoing development and iteration. Most clients stay – but the first version is the one that decides whether there's anything to iterate on.
faq.a8: Book the free call or send the form. We reply within 24 hours with relevant cases and an honest read on fit.

yachtmate.solution: We built YachtMate as an exclusive platform with member verification, role-based permissions, real-time chat, and event tools. React and Node.js power low-latency messaging while keeping member data private and access-controlled.

meta.title: SharingGround – P2P Item Sharing Platform | Ortvest
meta.description: How Ortvest built a peer-to-peer sharing platform with user verification, escrow payments, item tracking, and insurance integration.

hero.subtitle: A peer-to-peer platform that lets people lend and borrow items within their community – with built-in trust, tracking, and secure payments.

sharingground.challenge: Building a P2P sharing platform where strangers trust each other with their belongings. The core problem: how do you create accountability, prevent fraud, and handle disputes – without being the middleman for every transaction?
sharingground.solution: We built a trust layer from the ground up – identity verification, item condition logging, insurance integration, and a transparent review system. Payments are held in escrow and released only when both sides confirm the exchange.

sections.title: Purposes and Legal Bases for Processing

blocks.text: We process your data for the following purposes:
4.1 Responding to inquiries (contact form)
Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR – processing is necessary for taking steps at the request of the data subject prior to entering into a contract.
4.2 Direct marketing of our services (B2B)
Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR – legitimate interest of the Company (marketing own services to business clients).
4.3 Analytics and Website improvement
Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR – legitimate interest in understanding how the Website is used and improving user experience.
4.4 Legal obligations
Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR – compliance with applicable legal obligations (e.g., accounting, tax records).
4.5 Publishing and displaying client reviews
We process review form data to publish client testimonials on our Website, subject to moderation.

Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR – consent. By submitting the review form, you voluntarily provide data intended for public display. You may withdraw consent at any time by contacting contact@ortvest.com, and we will remove your review.
4.6 Evaluating partnership applications
We process partnership application data to assess whether a proposed engagement is a suitable fit, to respond to your application, and to prepare for potential contractual negotiations.
Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR – processing is necessary for taking steps at your request prior to entering into a contract.
Partnership application data is reviewed internally and is not published, shared with other applicants, or used for any purpose other than evaluating and responding to your application.
Our Website uses cookies and similar technologies. Cookies are small text files stored on your device.
We use:

items: Necessary cookies – required for the proper functioning of the Website
Analytics cookies – e.g., Google Analytics (to analyse traffic and usage patterns)
Marketing cookies – only if you have given explicit consent

blocks.text: You can manage cookie preferences through your browser settings or via our cookie consent banner. Refusing analytics or marketing cookies will not affect access to the Website.
We do not sell your personal data. We may share data with trusted third parties only to the extent necessary:

items: IT service providers and hosting companies (data processors under GDPR)
Email and CRM platforms (e.g., for managing inquiries)
Analytics providers (e.g., Google Analytics)
Legal, tax, or financial advisors, where required

blocks.text: All third-party processors are bound by data processing agreements in compliance with GDPR Art. 28.

Due to the international nature of our business, personal data may be transferred to and processed in countries outside the European Economic Area (EEA), including the United States and Ukraine. We ensure that all such transfers are carried out with appropriate safeguards as required by Chapter V of GDPR:
7.1 Transfers to the United States

Transfers to the US may occur via service providers (e.g., Google, cloud platforms). These transfers are carried out under Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) approved by the European Commission (Commission Decision 2021/914), and where applicable, supplementary technical and organisational measures to ensure an equivalent level of data protection.
7.2 Transfers to Ukraine

Ukraine is not listed among countries recognised by the European Commission as providing an adequate level of data protection. Where personal data is transferred to Ukraine (e.g., for development or operational purposes), we rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (Art. 46(2)(c) GDPR) and implement additional safeguards including data minimisation, encryption in transit and at rest, and access controls. Where required, we will seek your explicit consent for such transfers (Art. 49(1)(a) GDPR).
You may request a copy of the safeguards applied to international transfers by contacting us at contact@ortvest.com.
We retain your personal data for as long as necessary:

items: Inquiry data: up to 3 years from the last contact, or until you request deletion

Partnership application data: up to 12 months from submission where no engagement follows, or until you request deletion. Where an engagement begins, the data is retained under the client data period below.
Client data (if a contract is concluded): 5 years from the end of the business relationship (tax and accounting requirements)
Analytics data: as per the settings of the analytics provider (typically up to 26 months)
Review data: retained for as long as the review is published on the Website, or until you request deletion by contacting contact@ortvest.com

items: Right of access (Art. 15 GDPR) – obtain a copy of your data
Right to rectification (Art. 16 GDPR) – correct inaccurate data
Right to erasure / "right to be forgotten" (Art. 17 GDPR)
Right to restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR)
Right to data portability (Art. 20 GDPR)
Right to object to processing (Art. 21 GDPR) – including direct marketing
Right to withdraw consent at any time (where processing is based on consent)

blocks.text:
To exercise any of these rights, contact us at: contact@ortvest.com
We will respond within 30 days as required by GDPR Art. 12.
If you believe we are processing your data unlawfully, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Polish supervisory authority:

models.label: Engagement models
models.title: Three ways to work together beyond a standard contract

embedded.title: Embedded team
embedded.who: You have a product vision and need a full-stack squad without managing five separate vendors.
embedded.what: Engineering, design and go-to-market embedded into your team for the duration. One point of contact, one squad, weekly demos.
embedded.terms: Fixed-scope or rolling monthly. Rates on request.

equity.title: Build + equity
equity.who: You have validated demand but limited runway. You're willing to exchange equity for a lower burn rate.
equity.what: We build the platform at a reduced rate in exchange for a small equity stake. The split depends on scope and stage.
equity.terms: Equity 2–8% depending on scope. Minimum engagement 4 months.

cto.title: Technical co-founder function
cto.who: You're a non-technical founder who needs someone to own the tech – not just execute it.
cto.what: We act as your technical co-founder: architecture, vendor selection, team hiring, code review and build.
cto.terms: Retainer + equity. Structure defined per engagement.

notFor.label: Not for everyone
notFor.title: Who this isn't for
items: Founders who already have a team and need extra capacity
Projects that aren't two-sided – single-player apps, internal tools, pure SaaS
Founders who need a yes-man rather than someone who will push back on the spec
Timelines under 6 weeks – not enough time to do this properly

proof.label: Why us
proof.title: The part you shouldn't have to manage
proof.subtitle: You own the market, the customers and the calls only you can make. Everything between an idea and a running platform is ours.

1.title: A team deep enough not to be your bottleneck
1.body: Fifteen people, and the ones on your project aren't split across six others. Backend, product and go-to-market sit in one room – so the platform and the admin tooling get built in parallel, not one after the other while you wait.

2.title: We've made these calls with our own money
2.body: We fund Yachtly ourselves: pricing model, which side to seed first, which features to cut. That's why we argue about your business model instead of just implementing it. A studio that has never owned the downside will build whatever you ask for.

3.title: You don't need to know what to ask for
3.body: Architecture, stack, trade-offs, what breaks at scale, when to hire in-house – ours to get right. You bring the market and the decisions only you can make. Nobody hands you a repo and a good-luck email.
